question.problem:
An office typist was given the task to transfer all the work documents to the company's internal system. The following table shows some statistics on the process.

| **$t\,\text{(hour)}$** | $4\text{th}$ | $5\text{th}$ | $6\text{th}$ | $7\text{th}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${D}^{′}(t)\,\text{(documents/hour)}$ | $11$ | $8$ | $7$ | $10$ |

$$

$$

The typist transfers the documents at a rate of ${D}^{′}(t)$, where ${D}^{′}(t)$ is measured in documents per hour. At the end of the seventh hour, $t=7$, the typist had completed $50$ documents. Use the tangent line approximation of $D$ at time $t=7$ to determine the number of documents transferred after the ninth hour.
question.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $D(t)$ at the point $a=7$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(t) & =D(a)+{D}^{′}(a)(t-a) \\  & =D(7)+{D}^{′}(7)(t-7) \\  & =50+10(t-7).\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $D(9)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $t=9.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}D(9) & ≈L(9) \\  & =50+10(9-7) \\  & =50+10(2) \\  & =50+20 \\  & =70.\end{aligned}
$$
